Tasks: the same 20 procedurally generated scenarios (seeds) for all configurations, 100 turns each. Configurations: 7 models x 3 open harnesses (OpenCode, Mini-SWE, OpenHands) plus provider harnesses where available (26 cells). Baseline: none designated (R = 0 no-feedback as reference for the retry effect; Python/LLM sampling as reference for ablations). Held constant: scenarios, instructions (README.md), Python by default, Docker isolation, R = 2, detailed feedback; infrastructure retries up to 10 not counted. Acceptance tests: programmatic HTTP test suite per turn, hidden from the agent. Repetitions: one run per cell; OpenCode + Qwen3.5-122B repeated 5 times to estimate noise. Statistics: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank per scenario, Holm correction across cells. Human intervention: none

Without feedback all models fail within about 5-6 turns (best GLM-5 6.2). Retry loop (R = 2) improves all 26 cells significantly (Holm p < 0.05), up to 12x. Harness matters: OpenCode best or not significantly worse than best for all 7 models; OpenHands worst for 6/7; stronger models up to 6x gap between best and worst harness; provider harnesses do not reliably help (QwenCode significantly worse than OpenCode for Qwen3-Coder-Next p = 0.014 and Qwen3.5-122B p = 0.011). GLM-5 on OpenCode (57.0) significantly above all except Qwen3.5-122B (p = 0.07). Detailed vs minimal feedback 6-12x more turns, significant for 6/7. Rust lower (significant for 4 models); JavaScript not significantly different; programmatic vs LLM sampling not significant except Nemotron Super. Qwen3.5-122B most cost-efficient

Yes, partly: distinguished harnesses and models with paired tests (several significant differences) and showed retry and feedback effects; run-to-run noise estimated from 5 runs of one configuration (mean 32.4 ± 6.3 SD turns @3; per-run 23.3-39.4), comparable to some between-cell differences; one run per cell otherwise. Limitations stated: high cost (billions of tokens; closed models out of reach, about $13.6K Claude Sonnet 4.6 and $22.7K GPT-5.5 per configuration), K = 20 gives limited statistical power, one task type (REST API)

Limitations: multi-turn evaluation expensive, so no closed-source models evaluated; K = 20 scenarios may lack statistical power; single task type (REST API servers), findings may not hold in other domains. Gaps: multi-turn reliability of agents and harnesses (context compaction without losing instructions, recovery from infrastructure issues); agents need precise feedback that is often unavailable in practice; longer scenarios beyond 100 turns
